conceptual assets.concept: Outgoing DBUS request transaction (assembled bus_req_t sent to the data bus)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL composes the outgoing bus request record in mem_do_reg and other places: dbus_req_o.addr <= mar; mem_do_reg (when ctrl_i.lsu_mo_we='1') assigns dbus_req_o.rw <= ctrl_i.lsu_rw, dbus_req_o.priv <= ctrl_i.lsu_priv, dbus_req_o.debug <= ctrl_i.cpu_debug, dbus_req_o.amo <= ctrl_i.lsu_amo, dbus_req_o.amoop <= amo_cmd, dbus_req_o.data <= (wdata_i sliced/repeated per funct3 and addr_i), dbus_req_o.ben <= ...; dbus_req_o.stb <= ctrl_i.lsu_req and (not misaligned) and (not pmp_fault_i); bus_lock sets dbus_req_o.lock; dbus_req_o.fence <= ctrl_i.lsu_fence. These RTL assignments implement the transaction the LSU issues; corruption of any request field changes memory-access semantics, establishing an Integrity objective. Mapping note: the request is carried on the transport-style port dbus_req_o (a bus_req_t record); transport ports and their fields are excluded from structural reporting, so no eligible internal declaration represents the whole outgoing transaction (structural list is empty).

conceptual assets.concept: Incoming DBUS response transaction (ack, data, err)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL consumes the incoming response record dbus_rsp_i to progress LSU flows: access_arbiter clears pending on dbus_rsp_i.ack = '1' and mem_di_reg reads dbus_rsp_i.data to form rdata_o (cases selecting bytes by mar and funct3 and applying replicate_f for sign-extension); err_o bits use dbus_rsp_i.err. These response fields determine ack, returned data and reported errors; their integrity is required for correct LSU behavior. Mapping note: dbus_rsp_i is a transport-style port (bus_rsp_t) and transport ports/fields are excluded from structural reporting, so no eligible internal declaration represents the whole incoming response (structural list is empty).

conceptual assets.concept: Memory access address stored in MAR
conceptual assets.reasoning: mem_addr_reg stores the requested address when the core writes MAR: on rising_edge clk_i if ctrl_i.lsu_mo_we = '1' then mar <= addr_i; the RTL then drives dbus_req_o.addr <= mar and mar_o <= mar; mem_di_reg uses mar to select response bytes when assembling rdata_o. The stored MAR therefore directly determines which memory location is accessed and which response bytes are selected; corruption of MAR violates address integrity. Structural realizations: MAR is retained internally (mar stores), exported from the entity (mar_o exit port), and is set from the input address (addr_i sets) under the write-enable control (ctrl_i sets).

mem_addr_reg computes and stores misaligned from the instruction width fields and address bits when MAR is written: case ctrl_i.ir_funct3(1 downto 0) is '00' => misaligned<='0'; '01' => misaligned<=addr_i(0); others => misaligned<=addr_i(1) or addr_i(0). misaligned is then used to gate the strobe (dbus_req_o.stb <= ctrl_i.lsu_req and (not misaligned) and (not pmp_fault_i)) and to generate err_o(0)/err_o(2). An incorrect misaligned value would wrongly permit/block requests or assert/clear error flags, establishing Integrity. Structural realizations: misaligned is stored (misaligned stores) and depends on the input controls/address (ctrl_i sets, addr_i sets).

access_arbiter implements in-flight state: on reset pending<='0'; on rising_edge when pending='0' pending <= ctrl_i.lsu_req; when dbus_rsp_i.ack='1' or ctrl_i.cpu_trap='1' pending <= '0'. pending gates result capture (mem_di_reg uses 'if (pending = '1') then ...') and is used in err_o and lock-release logic. The pending flag implements the in-progress transaction arbitration; corruption of pending breaks arbitration, data capture and error reporting, establishing Integrity. Structural realizations: pending is stored internally (pending stores) and is set from the control input that requests accesses (ctrl_i sets).

conceptual assets.concept: PMP fault indicator used by LSU
conceptual assets.reasoning: access_arbiter samples the external PMP fault input into pmp_err: on rising_edge pmp_err <= pmp_fault_i. The PMP fault is used to block requests (dbus_req_o.stb uses (not pmp_fault_i)) and to report errors (err_o(1)/err_o(3) include (dbus_rsp_i.err or pmp_err)). The stored PMP-fault state therefore controls whether accesses proceed and whether protection faults are reported; corruption of this state misrepresents protection faults, establishing Integrity. Structural realizations: pmp_err is stored internally (pmp_err stores) and originates from the input (pmp_fault_i sets).

amo_encode is a combinational mapping from ctrl_i.ir_funct12(11 downto 7) to the 4-bit amo_cmd (examples: '00010' => '1000', '00011' => '1001', others => '0000'); mem_do_reg places that value into the outgoing transaction via dbus_req_o.amoop <= amo_cmd. The computed amo_cmd defines the atomic operation encoded into the request; incorrect encoding changes AMO semantics, establishing Integrity. Structural realizations: amo_cmd is the computed internal signal (amo_cmd computes) derived from control input (ctrl_i sets).

mem_di_reg produces rdata_o when pending='1': case ctrl_i.ir_funct3 selects byte/half/word extraction from dbus_rsp_i.data using mar(1 downto 0) and applies replicate_f((not ctrl_i.ir_funct3(2)) and dbus_rsp_i.data(...), ...) for sign-extension, otherwise rdata_o <= dbus_rsp_i.data. The value driven on rdata_o is the data returned to the core; corruption of rdata_o changes the value the CPU reads, establishing Integrity. Structural realization: rdata_o is the entity output through which the value leaves (rdata_o exit port).

The RTL drives the error output vector explicitly: err_o(0) <= pending and (not ctrl_i.lsu_rw) and misaligned; err_o(1) <= pending and (not ctrl_i.lsu_rw) and (dbus_rsp_i.err or pmp_err); err_o(2) <= pending and ctrl_i.lsu_rw and misaligned; err_o(3) <= pending and ctrl_i.lsu_rw and (dbus_rsp_i.err or pmp_err). These outputs report access/response error conditions; their integrity is required so control/firmware see correct fault status. Structural realization: err_o is the entity output carrying the reported flags (err_o exit port).

The RTL drives wait_o <= not dbus_rsp_i.ack. The wait_o output signals bus-response readiness to other logic; corruption of wait_o would misstate response readiness and break stall/wait behavior, establishing Integrity. Structural realization: wait_o is the entity output that leaves the block (wait_o exit port).
